load_component.component_id: The component's unique ID from `available_components`, rather than its name or file path.

load_skill.skill_id: The skill's unique ID from `available_skills`, rather than its name or file path.

read_resource.slide_id: Stable unique slide ID from the current outline.
read_resource.type: `manifest` for global content requirements; `design` for global visual requirements; `outline` for the presentation's sections, subsections, and slides; `spec` for semantic content plan; `html` for exact source.

read_image.attachment_id: Uploaded unique image ID from attachment context, rather than a file path or URL.
read_image.slide_id: Stable unique slide ID from the current outline, rather than a file path or URL.

render_slide.assess_quality: `true` requests an additional slide quality assessment; `false` only returns the screenshot and diagnostics.
render_slide.slide_id: Stable unique slide ID from the current outline.

edit_manifest.audience: A concise description of the presentation's target audience, guiding content depth and terminology complexity.
edit_manifest.goal: A concise statement of the presentation's purpose, focusing on what the audience should understand or be able to do.
edit_manifest.language: The language used in the presentation, specified as a language tag such as `en-US` or `zh-CN`.
edit_manifest.slide_count: The desired number of slides in the presentation, which may be a range or an approximation.
edit_manifest.prohibitions: Each item specifies a concrete content restriction tailored to this presentation and shared across slides.
edit_manifest.requirements: Each item specifies a concrete content requirement tailored to this presentation and shared across slides.
edit_manifest.title: A concise title for the entire presentation that captures its main theme, scope, and content.

edit_design.prohibitions: Each item specifies a concrete visual restriction tailored to this presentation and shared across slides.
edit_design.requirements: Each item specifies a concrete visual requirement tailored to this presentation and shared across slides.

edit_spec.core: A concise statement of the main takeaway the audience should retain from this slide, rather than its title, a content inventory or layout instructions.
edit_spec.elements: The complete ordered list of semantic content units for this slide; order follows how the audience should read them.
edit_spec.elements.intent: A concise statement of the concrete message, facts, evidence or relationship this element should convey and why it belongs on this slide.
edit_spec.elements.type: `text` for prose; `list` for items; `metric` for a key figure; `quote` for a quotation; `table` for tabular values; `chart` for data visualization; `diagram` for relationships; `code` for a code sample; `asset` for visual media.
edit_spec.layout: A concise statement of how content is spatially arranged to improve visual appeal and readability, rather than specific HTML or CSS implementation details.
edit_spec.purpose: `cover` for topic and identity; `introduction` for background, problem, goals or structure; `transition` for a chapter change; `content_explanation` for concepts or facts; `content_comparison` for differences or tradeoffs; `content_example` for concrete cases; `content_guidance` for methods or recommendations; `content_other` for a known body-content mode outside these categories; `conclusion` for summary, conclusions or actions; `other` for a known page role outside these categories. Choose the dominant purpose for mixed content.
edit_spec.slide_id: Stable unique slide ID from the current outline.

edit_outline.content: Complete outline JSON source to create or fully replace the outline, without Markdown fences.
edit_outline.edits: Ordered exact text replacements in the current saved outline JSON source.
edit_outline.edits.new_text: Literal replacement source; use an empty string to delete the matched text.
edit_outline.edits.old_text: Exact, non-empty source text to replace, including whitespace and enough surrounding context to identify one occurrence.

edit_html.content: The complete HTML document to create or replace, without Markdown fences.
edit_html.edits: The ordered list of exact text replacements to apply to the current saved HTML.
edit_html.edits.new_text: The literal replacement source; use an empty string to delete the matched text.
edit_html.edits.old_text: The exact, non-empty source text to replace, including whitespace.
edit_html.slide_id: Stable unique slide ID from the current outline.

create_plan.content: Markdown explanation of the request, implementation approach, relevant constraints and expected outcomes. Do not include the execution step list.
create_plan.steps: Complete ordered execution steps, each a concise sentence describing one action or deliverable. This is the sole source for approval and progress displays.
create_plan.title: User-facing title of the proposed work.

update_plan.updates: Status changes for existing approved steps.
update_plan.updates.status: `pending` for work awaiting execution; `processing` for work in progress; `completed` for finished work that achieved its expected result; `failed` for work whose execution failed.
update_plan.updates.step_id: Exact unique step ID from the current plan context.

request_privilege.reason: User-facing explanation of why the authorized slide scope needs to be expanded.
request_privilege.slide_ids: IDs of the slides to add to the current authorized scope.

ask_user.questions: Ordered questions to present together, each addressing one fact or decision.
ask_user.questions.options: One to three preset answers for a single-choice question; custom text is always available. Omit this field or pass `[]` to show a text input instead.
ask_user.questions.options.description: Concrete meaning, effect or tradeoff of this option.
ask_user.questions.options.label: Concise and distinct option text. If you strongly recommend this option, append `(Recommended)` to its end.
ask_user.questions.question: Complete user-visible interrogative sentence, ending with question mark.
ask_user.questions.reason: Brief user-visible explanation of why the answer is needed and what subsequent work it affects.

review_ppt.demand: Self-contained instructions for the reviewer, including the review objective, key areas to focus on, acceptance criteria, relevant user requirements and decisions, and the feedback you need.

suggest_request.requests: Zero to three distinct single-line plain-text requests the user is likely to make next, inferred from the conversation, current project and completed work. Each is a self-contained ready-to-send sentence matching the user's language and wording.

git_commit.items: Distinct body entries, each summarizing one coherent change in a single sentence.
git_commit.title: Concise single-line plain-text title that summarizes the primary change, in the format `<feat|fix|refactor|perf|chore|docs>: <primary change>`, without Markdown, HTML, surrounding quotation marks, status prefixes, or a trailing period.

run_command.command: Bash source to execute from the project directory.

rename_thread.action: `rename` for a missing title or one that no longer represents the recent main topic; `keep` for a title that still fits or when the available information is insufficient to choose a better one.
rename_thread.title: Concise single-line plain-text title that identifies the conversation's main topic or current stage of work, without Markdown, HTML, surrounding quotation marks, status prefixes, or a trailing period.

compact_context.content: Complete Markdown working summary for continuing the same task.
compact_context.title: Concise single-line plain-text title that identifies the task, stage, or key decision captured in the summary, without Markdown, HTML, surrounding quotation marks, status prefixes, or a trailing period.

polish_instruction.content: Complete revised draft ready to send, or the original draft if no changes are needed.
polish_instruction.title: Concise single-line plain-text title that describes the wording improvement or indicates that the draft is unchanged, without Markdown, HTML, surrounding quotation marks, status prefixes, or a trailing period.

handoff_thread.content: Complete standalone Markdown handoff brief, ready to send as the first message to the receiving Agent.
handoff_thread.title: Concise single-line plain-text title that identifies the work or stage being handed over, without Markdown, HTML, surrounding quotation marks, status prefixes, or a trailing period.
